# Telegram Media Downloader

> Self-hosted Telegram media downloader with a web dashboard. It downloads and archives photos, videos, documents, voice messages, GIFs, stickers and Stories from Telegram channels, groups and private chats (including private ones you belong to) using your own account over MTProto. Version 3.x is a single Go binary, tgdl-server, with the dashboard embedded; it runs from the Docker image ghcr.io/botnick/telegram-media-downloader (amd64, arm64) or as a native binary on Linux, Windows and macOS. MIT licensed.

Key facts for 3.x (current 3.4): no Node.js runtime; Telegram via gotd; state in SQLite under TGDL_DATA_DIR (./data), media optionally under TGDL_DOWNLOADS_DIR; dashboard on port 3000; first password set with `tgdl-server setup --password-stdin`; 2.x installs upgrade in place. Since 3.4 the 2.x background features are back: auto-forward, self-destructing (TTL) media capture, disk rotation (deletes the oldest downloads over diskManagement.maxTotalSize), periodic integrity sweep, Google Drive and Dropbox backups (`tgdl-server backup-oauth`), cluster dedup sweep, backfill date window, FFMPEG_HWACCEL, real /metrics. Also: adaptive download concurrency (advanced.downloader), FloodWait protection, self-restarting monitor with a watchdog, scheduled watchtower updates, built-in seekbar previews. Face recognition needs the tgdl-faces container (FACES_SERVICE_URL / TGDL_FACES_SIDECAR_URL) and NSFW scoring the tgdl-nsfw container (TGDL_NSFW_SIDECAR_URL); there is no local face-sidecar mode and no in-process NSFW model.

## Quick answers

- What it is: a free, MIT-licensed, self-hosted app that downloads media from Telegram channels, groups and chats with your own user account (not a bot). Website: https://botnick.github.io/telegram-media-downloader/ (Thai: https://botnick.github.io/telegram-media-downloader/th/).
- Install: `docker compose up -d` with the repository's docker-compose.yml, then `tgdl-server setup --password-stdin` for the first password; open http://localhost:3000. Needs a free apiId/apiHash from my.telegram.org.
- Private channels: yes, if the signed-in account is a member.
- Download a whole channel: Chats > pick the channel > backfill (0 = all messages); turn on the realtime monitor to keep it current.
- Single message or Stories: paste a t.me link, or look up Stories by username.
- Platforms: Docker amd64/arm64; release binaries for Linux (amd64, arm64, arm), Windows and macOS; Synology compose file included.
- Duplicates: skipped before download by Telegram media identity, confirmed by SHA-256; optional "Skip duplicates" setting stops repeat library entries.
- Upgrading from 2.x: in place, same image, port, data folder and logins.
- Latest version and release notes: https://github.com/botnick/telegram-media-downloader/releases/latest and CHANGELOG.md.

## Code map

- core-service/cmd/tgdl-server: the server plus `setup`, `backup-restore`, `backup-decrypt`, `backup-oauth` and `version` commands
- core-service/internal/app: HTTP and WebSocket routes, authorization, settings, integration
- core-service/internal/accounts, telegram, session: account ownership, gotd sessions, login, Telegram updates
- core-service/internal/engine, download, filepublish: durable queue, ingestion, download-time dedup, streaming SHA-256, atomic publication and recovery
- core-service/internal/store, dbread: SQLite schema, migrations and read projections
- core-service/internal/backup, cluster, rescue: backups and restore, peer pairing and sync, rescue retention
- core-service/internal/webassets/public: browser dashboard (ES modules) embedded in the binary
- Build and test with `make build`, `make test`, `make check`. Historical HTTP/WS contract snapshots are in tests/contract; the removed Node backend is in Git at commit aa83eed. faces-service (tgdl-faces) and nsfw-service (tgdl-nsfw) are separate sidecar projects the server calls over HTTP; seekbar-service is no longer used (sprites are built in the server).
